passage: I'm Rukmini, and I share a pod with Kamal and Harish. After the quarterly review where Harish presented the vendor plan alone, Kamal said nothing in the meeting. Not a word. But at the tea machine he told me, 'Our plan, his applause. Typical.' Since then I've noticed things. Kamal's emails to Harish have shrunk to one line: 'Done.' 'See attached.' Last week Harish asked where the updated supplier list was, and Kamal said, 'Not sure,' though I'd seen it open on his screen that morning. Harish came to me later, confused. 'What did I do? He's so cold with me.' I don't know what Kamal feels inside. I only know the room has gone quiet between them.

qa.q: What did Kamal tell Rukmini at the tea machine?
qa.a: He told her, 'Our plan, his applause. Typical.'

qa.q: What might Kamal's 'Not sure' about the supplier list reveal about his feelings?
qa.a: It suggests hidden resentment toward Harish, showing up as withheld information rather than saying openly that he felt slighted.

qa.q: What could break this cycle of silent resentment?
qa.a: Kamal could tell Harish directly and calmly that he felt left out of the credit, instead of venting to Rukmini and going cold.

qa.q: How is Harish experiencing Kamal's cooler tone?
qa.a: He is confused and reads it as hostility without knowing what he did, which may make him defensive too.

grounding: A colleague notices a man who stayed silent in the meeting complain afterwards, then send short emails and withhold information that his teammate reads as hostility.

Monday. In the sprint review, Arohi thanked 'the whole team' for the launch while her name sat alone on the release notes. Kamal, who had fixed the checkout bug at 2 a.m., said nothing. At lunch he told Bilal, 'She'll take credit for the sunrise next.'
Thursday. Arohi messaged, 'Can you send the test logs? Need them for the client.' Kamal replied an hour later: 'Sent.' Only half the logs were attached.
The following Tuesday. Arohi stopped by his desk. 'Is something wrong? Your emails feel hostile.' Kamal kept his eyes on his screen. 'Everything's fine. Just busy.' She walked away, arms crossed. He felt a small, sour satisfaction, and underneath it, something uneasy.

qa.q: What had Kamal fixed at 2 a.m.?
qa.a: Kamal had fixed the checkout bug at 2 a.m.

qa.q: What does the 'small, sour satisfaction' with something uneasy underneath suggest about Kamal?
qa.a: Part of him enjoys punishing Arohi quietly, but he also senses that his hidden resentment is harming the working relationship.

qa.q: When Arohi asked 'Is something wrong?', what turning point did Kamal miss?
qa.a: He could have said honestly that he felt uncredited for the bug fix; that one sentence might have cleared the air instead of deepening the hostility.

qa.q: How does Arohi read Kamal's half-sent logs and short replies?
qa.a: She reads them as hostility without knowing the cause, which leaves her hurt and defensive, arms crossed.

grounding: Over a week a man who said nothing about missing credit vents to a colleague, then sends short replies and half the logs, which his teammate reads as hostility.

The cooperative dairy office in Anand had one fan and four desks. After Monday's meeting, where Zeenat presented the milk-collection figures without mentioning his route survey, Vishal said nothing. He smiled and passed the biscuits.
At lunch, by the chai stall, he told Ravi, "She takes everything. You'll see."
Over the week, his emails to Zeenat shrank. "Noted." "Will check." When she asked for the village list, he sent it a day late, without the phone numbers she needed.
On Friday Zeenat asked quietly, "Vishal, have I done something? You seem angry with me."
"Angry? No. Just busy," he said, and turned back to his screen.

qa.q: What did Vishal's emails to Zeenat shrink to?
qa.a: "Noted." "Will check."

qa.q: What was Vishal feeling underneath "Just busy"?
qa.a: He felt resentful and hurt at being left out of the presentation, but was hiding it behind a cooler tone.

qa.q: What turning point could Vishal take instead of withholding information?
qa.a: Telling Zeenat directly that he felt left out of the credit, since she has already opened the door by asking.

qa.q: What is Zeenat experiencing as Vishal's emails shrink?
qa.a: She feels confused and uneasy, reading his coolness as hostility without knowing the reason.

grounding: Shows a man who says nothing in the meeting, complains to a colleague, and lets resentment leak into short emails and withheld details.

passage:
In the London logistics office, Kofi said nothing when Dalia's report went to the director with only her name on it. He had done the supplier analysis. He nodded through the meeting, then complained to Tom at the coffee machine: "Classic Dalia."
After that, his replies to her were one line. When she asked for the updated delivery times, he sent last week's file. When she said "Good morning," he said "Morning" without looking up.
On Thursday Dalia found Tom in the kitchen. "Is Kofi okay? He's been really cold to me. I think he hates me."
Tom shrugged awkwardly and stirred his tea.

qa.q: What did Kofi send when Dalia asked for the updated delivery times?
qa.a: Last week's file.

qa.q: Why did Kofi say "Classic Dalia" at the coffee machine?
qa.a: He felt resentful and overlooked about the report, and vented it to Tom instead of to Dalia.

qa.q: What went wrong in how Kofi handled his hurt, and what could fix it?
qa.a: He hid it and leaked it through cold replies and old files; a direct, calm word with Dalia about credit could fix it.

qa.q: What is it like for Dalia to receive Kofi's cold replies?
qa.a: She feels hurt and confused, reading his coolness as hatred without knowing why.

grounding: Shows a man who stays silent in the meeting but vents to a colleague, with resentment showing in cold replies and withheld information.

passage:
In the school staffroom, Gautam marked papers while the principal praised Baljeet's new science club plan in the staff meeting. Gautam had suggested the idea in June. Nobody mentioned it. He said nothing.
Afterwards, at the tea urn, he muttered to the maths teacher, "Some people are good at collecting credit."
The next week Baljeet asked for the lab timetable. Gautam sent it without the Saturday slots. Baljeet's messages got "ok" in reply, nothing more.
On Wednesday Baljeet sat down beside him. "Gautam, you've been different with me. Did I do something?"
Gautam kept marking. "Not everything is about you, Baljeet."

qa.q: What did Gautam leave out of the lab timetable?
qa.a: The Saturday slots.

qa.q: What was Gautam feeling during the staff meeting?
qa.a: He felt overlooked and resentful that his June idea went unmentioned, but kept it to himself.

qa.q: What could Gautam do instead of answering "Not everything is about you"?
qa.a: Accept Baljeet's opening and say calmly that he had suggested the idea in June and felt left out.

qa.q: How might Baljeet be experiencing Gautam's replies?
qa.a: Baljeet is probably confused and hurt, reading the coldness as hostility without knowing the cause.

grounding: Shows a teacher who stays silent in a meeting, complains to a colleague, and lets resentment show in short replies and withheld details.

passage:
Subject: Need to vent

Hi Nikhil,
Remember Damini taking the lead on the vendor audit? In Monday's review the director praised "Damini's framework", which was half mine. I said nothing. Just smiled. Afterwards I spent twenty minutes ranting to Joel in the pantry.
Since then I've been replying to her in one line. Today she asked for the vendor contacts list and I wrote, "Will check." I had the list open in another tab. I know that's petty. She messaged Joel asking if I was angry with her, he told me, and honestly part of me was glad she'd noticed.
I don't like who I'm being this week, but I don't know how to say any of it without sounding small.
Darshan

qa.q: How did Darshan reply when Damini asked for the vendor contacts list?
qa.a: Darshan wrote only "Will check," with the list already open in another tab.

qa.q: What mix of feelings shows in Darshan's email?
qa.a: Darshan feels resentful about the lost credit, a little glad Damini noticed, and ashamed of acting petty.

qa.q: What could Darshan do instead of the one-line replies?
qa.a: Darshan could send the list and ask Damini for a short talk about how the framework was credited, naming the problem directly.

qa.q: How does Damini seem to read the cooler tone?
qa.a: She reads it as anger aimed at her, enough to ask Joel about it, without knowing the real cause.

grounding: Shows unspoken resentment after lost credit leaking into one-line replies, withheld information and a cooler tone the colleague reads as hostility.
